title: three-day-landing-sprint-onboard-kit-wip
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, experiment-first onboarding kit for new ICs joining product and platform teams where we want early concrete contributions. Focus: compress meaningful orientation into a repeatable 3-day landing sprint that combines access, context, and a first small deliverable.

Audience:
- Hiring managers and onboarding POCs who want a rapid, low-friction landing plan.
- Interviewers who need a matching evidence capture protocol for the first-week assignment.

Goals:
- New hire completes a scoped technical task with reviewer feedback within 3 business days.
- Collect standardized interview-to-onboard evidence that maps candidate interview signals to actual early performance.
- Surface friction points (access, infra, docs) within 48 hours and escalate to SRE/Platform.

Scope / Not included:
- This is not a replacement for the full 90-day onboarding program; handoff to the 30/60/90 cadence happens after day 3.
- Not for senior manager hires (separate leadership onboarding).

Preboarding (Day -3 to Day 0):
- People ops sends prepping packet (account checklist, team chart, artifact links).
- Manager assigns a Day 1 buddy and picks a 3-day landing issue from the backlog tagged "3-day-landing".
- Infra work: request ephemeral dev access, repo perms, test dataset provisioning (owner: infra oncall).
- Quick self-check: new hire confirms access by Day 0 5pm PST.

Three-day schedule (high level):
Day 1 — Orientation + Micro-task kickoff
- 09:00 intro sync (manager + buddy) 30 mins: context, team goals, what success looks like for 3 days.
- 10:00 environment onboarding (buddy-led) 60 mins: repo clone, tokens, test data, local run.
- 13:00 tiny design review: 30 mins to agree scope on the landing issue.
- Afternoon: first PR skeleton / exploratory tests.
- Evidence to capture: notes on setup friction, time-to-first-run (minutes).

Day 2 — Deep work + pairing
- Morning asynchronous deep work on task (owner: new hire).
- Dedicated 2-hour pairing window with buddy for troubleshooting.
- End-of-day informal sync: quick demo of progress.
- Evidence to capture: specific blockers, debugging steps, links to failing test logs.

Day 3 — Finish + review + retro
- Morning: finalize PR, ensure CI passes, add short README or playbook note.
- 11:00 formal review with manager + reviewer (30–45 mins).
- 16:00 15-min retro with people ops + manager: capture signals and escalate infra/Docs gaps.
- Handoff: add tasks to 30-day plan and schedule 1:1 onboarding topics.

Deliverable examples (choose one):
- Fix a flaky test and document repro steps + mitigation proposal.
- Add a small telemetry metric and a dashboard tile with narrative.
- Add a runnable example + README that reproduces a common bug for a feature.

Interview-to-onboard evidence protocol (how interview ratings map to early signals):
- We want to correlate interview rubrics to actual ramp signals; capture standardized artifact links during the 3-day sprint.
- Evidence items to attach to new hire record: PR link, short reviewer notes (bullet list), time-to-first-run (minutes), top-2 blockers and how resolved.
- Store in HR onboarding doc under "3-day-evidence".

Suggested quick rubric for the landing task (12 point scale):
- Setup (0–3): can they get a local/dev environment running? Notes: time and key missing perms.
- Problem understanding (0–3): restates the task, proposes sensible approach.
- Implementation + code hygiene (0–3): completes task, tests added, clear commit message.
- Communication / collaboration (0–3): asks clarifying questions, pairs effectively, documents decisions.
Recommend: pass threshold = 8/12 for confident continuation to standard ramp. If 6–7, schedule focused pairing + 1 week extension. If <=5, manager + people ops review for more structured remediation.

Interviewer guidance (to be added to candidate packet):
- For offers where we plan a 3-day landing sprint, explicitly tell candidate what to expect in offer letter addendum.
- Screening interviews should note any specific infra tools candidate lacks familiarity with (e.g., k8s, Terraform) — use that to scope the landing task.

Checklist (one-page) — copyable for team docs:
- [ ] Preboarding packet sent
- [ ] Day 1 buddy assigned
- [ ] Landing issue chosen and documented
- [ ] Access requested and validated
- [ ] Reviewer assigned for Day 3
- [ ] Evidence links created and stored
- [ ] Day 3 retro scheduled

Common friction patterns and mitigations (observed in trial runs):
- Missing repo perms: create "access fast-track" process with infra to grant read-only in 4 hours.
- Long-running CI: provide local mock or smoke test so new hire can validate quickly.
- Over-scoped tasks: prefer a clearly delimited slice with measurable acceptance criteria.

Open questions / decisions (WIP):
- Billing: do we want to bill manager team for buddy hours vs. central people ops? Decision owner: People Ops Director.
- Senior hires: do we run a modified 1-week landing sprint or skip? Owner: Head of Eng.
- Data-sensitive repos: what is minimum safe dataset for local dev? Owner: Security.

Next steps and short owners:
- Run a 3-team pilot in Q2: Product infra, Serving runtime, Console UX. Owner: Sofia Martinez (people ops). Deadline: 2025-03-15.
- Build a one-click onboarding checklist template in Confluence. Owner: Liam Chen.
- Add automated evidence capture links to offer acceptance flow (engineer infra ticket). Owner: Aisha Kapoor.

Notes to self:
- Keep scope small; the most useful output is a runnable demo or a clear CI passing PR.
- Capture the human signals (how they communicate blockers) as much as code metrics.

Relevant refs and quick links:
- Confluence playbook (draft): confluence/PEOPLE-ONBOARD-3DSPL-2025
- Pilot backlog label: jira:HR-789
- Slack thread for pilot coordination: #people-ops-onboarding

End.
